processes.name: GeneralDynamicModelProcess
processes.description:
One oceanic island under the General Dynamic Model (Whittaker et al. 2008).

Identical colonization/extinction bookkeeping to
:class:`~viva_island_biogeography.processes.MacArthurWilsonEquilibriumProcess`
— a mainland pool of ``n_pool`` species, each present (1) or absent (0);
every absent species colonizes with probability ``c = colonization_base`` and
every present species goes extinct with probability ``e(t)`` — **except** the
island's area is time-varying to model ontogeny. Each update advances the
island's own tick counter, evaluates ``area(t)`` from
:func:`gdm_area`, and recomputes
``e(t) = extinction_base·(ref_area/area(t))**area_exponent`` from the current
area (larger area => lower extinction). The instantaneous equilibrium
``S*(t)=P·c/(c+e(t))`` is therefore humped, and richness chases it with a lag
— producing the predicted overshoot-then-decline.

Outputs (deltas, so the stores accumulate to absolute values):

presence : map[string, float]
    Per-species occupancy delta (+1 colonization, -1 extinction).
richness : float
    Change in present-species count; the float store accumulates to the
    absolute richness.
area : float
    Change in island area versus the previous tick; the float store
    accumulates to the absolute ``area(t)`` so the viz can plot area directly.

processes.name: IslandProcess
processes.description:
A single island's time-stepped discrete Lotka-Volterra dynamics.

One ``update`` call == one generation (the model is discrete-time; the
``interval`` magnitude is not used to subdivide the map — set the composite's
process ``interval`` to 1.0 and run ``N`` steps for ``N`` generations).

Inputs
------
abundance : map[string, float]
    Current per-species counts on this island (read from the shared store).
immigration : map[string, float]
    External arrivals a sibling process may inject this tick (per species).
    Folded straight into the emitted abundance delta; defaults to empty, so
    with nothing wired it has no effect. (The archipelago's own inter-island
    migration is applied by :class:`MigrationProcess` directly to the shared
    abundance store, so this port is free for external couplers.)
growth_modifier : float
    Multiplies the island's mean growth rate (an environmental knob a sibling
    could drive); defaults to 1.0.

Outputs
-------
abundance : map[string, float]
    Per-species **delta** (post-step absolute minus pre-step current, plus
    any injected immigration and this island's random introductions). Emitted
    as a bare ``map[string,float]`` so it composes additively with
    :class:`MigrationProcess` and any sibling.
richness : float
    Delta of this island's local species richness (count of species with
    count > 0), emitted against the previous reading so the ``float`` store
    accumulates to the correct absolute value (the mass/length delta
    precedent). This is the island's *local* view (LV + introductions +
    injected immigration); the authoritative archipelago richness is derived
    from the full abundance store in the study runners.

processes.name: MacArthurWilsonEquilibriumProcess
processes.description:
One island under the canonical MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium model.

The phenomenological colonization/extinction model of *The Theory of Island
Biogeography* (MacArthur & Wilson 1963, 1967), as a counterpart to the
mechanistic Lotka-Volterra :class:`IslandProcess`. A mainland pool of
``n_pool`` species feeds the island; each species is present (1) or absent
(0). Each generation every absent species colonizes with probability
``c = colonization_base / (1 + distance)`` and every present species goes
extinct with probability ``e = extinction_base * (ref_area/area)**area_exponent``.

Richness relaxes to S* = P*c/(c+e): larger area (lower ``e``) and lower
isolation (higher ``c``) both raise it, and species identity turns over even
once S has plateaued (the turnover prediction). Immigration I(S)=(P-S)c
falls with S and extinction E(S)=S*e rises with S; they cross at S* — the
rate-crossing diagram.

Outputs (all deltas, so the stores accumulate to absolute values — the
mass/length delta precedent used throughout this workspace):

presence : map[string, float]
    Per-species occupancy delta (+1 colonization, -1 extinction); the store
    accumulates to a 0/1 occupancy vector.
richness : float
    Local richness delta; accumulates to the absolute present-species count.
cum_colonizations, cum_extinctions : float
    Per-tick gross colonization / extinction counts, emitted as deltas so
    the stores accumulate to running totals (their first difference per tick
    is the gross turnover, from which the per-S event rates are measured).

processes.name: MigrationProcess
processes.description:
The metacommunity migration coupler (port of ``IslandManager.simulate``'s
inter-island migration loop).

Reads every island's abundance and position, and for each ordered island
pair ``(i, j)`` with ``i != j`` moves a single randomly-chosen present
species from ``i`` to ``j`` with probability ``migration_rate(distance_ij)``
where ``distance_ij`` is the Euclidean distance between the islands and
``migration_rate(d) = 1/(1+d)`` — exactly the reference. The resulting
single-individual ``emigrate``/``immigrate`` adjustments are emitted as
abundance deltas keyed by island name, which compose additively with each
:class:`IslandProcess`'s own LV delta on the shared abundance store.

Inputs
------
abundances : map[string, map[string,float]]
    The whole archipelago abundance tree ``{island_name: {species: count}}``.

Outputs
-------
exchange : map[string, map[string,float]]
    Per-island per-species migration **deltas** ``{island_name: {species:
    +/-n}}`` (negative = emigration, positive = immigration).

processes.name: NeutralMetacommunityProcess
processes.description:
One island under Hubbell's (2001) zero-sum neutral metacommunity.

A fixed-size ``J = max(1, round(area * density))`` local community evolves by
``J`` Moran death/replacement events per generation (see module docstring).
Species are ecologically equivalent; richness and the species-abundance
distribution emerge from dispersal-drift balance, not from niche or rate
differences.

Inputs
------
abundance : map[string, float]
    Current per-species counts on this island (read from the shared store;
    seeded with ``J`` immigrants by the composite builder). Sums to ``J``.

Outputs (deltas, so the stores accumulate to absolute values)
-------
abundance : map[string, float]
    Net per-species count change over this generation's ``J`` events.
richness : float
    Local richness delta (species present now minus the previously recorded
    count), emitted against the previous reading so the ``float`` store
    telescopes to the current number of species present.

processes.name: RescueEffectProcess
processes.description:
One island under the MacArthur-Wilson model *with* the rescue effect.

Identical to :class:`MacArthurWilsonEquilibriumProcess` (presence/absence of
``n_pool`` pool species on a single island; absent species colonize at
``c = colonization_base/(1+distance)``; present species go extinct at the
area-dependent base ``e``) **except** that the incoming colonization pressure
also rescues present populations: each tick a present species is rescued with
probability ``c`` and, if rescued, its extinction probability is reduced to
``e*(1 - rescue_strength)``.

Outputs mirror :class:`MacArthurWilsonEquilibriumProcess` exactly (all
deltas, so the stores accumulate — the mass/length delta precedent), which
lets the study reuse :func:`viva_island_biogeography.viz.turnover_timeseries`
and :func:`viva_island_biogeography.viz.mw_rate_crossing` unchanged.

processes.name: JSONEmitter
processes.description:
Append simulation state to a persistent JSON Lines file each timestep.

Each recorded tick is one JSON object on its own line (``.json`` file in
JSON Lines / ``jsonl`` form). This is an append-only O(1)-per-tick write:
the previous behaviour re-read and re-serialized the entire history on
every tick (O(n) per tick -> O(n^2) per run), which dominated long runs.

``query`` transparently reads BOTH the current line-delimited format and
the legacy single JSON-array format, so files written by older versions
remain readable.

processes.name: KnowledgeStep
processes.description:
Step base class.

A `Step` is a stateless, non-temporal computational unit within a composite process.
It is triggered when its data dependencies are satisfied, functioning like a reaction
or transformation rule.

Override the `.update()` method to define custom behavior.

Override `.triggers()` to control which input ports trigger the step.
By default all inputs trigger — the step runs whenever any input changes.
To make some inputs "silent" (received but not triggering), return only
the triggering subset from `triggers()`.

Class attributes for memoization:
    ``_cache`` — ``'none'`` (default) or ``'by_hash'``. When
        ``'by_hash'``, ``invoke()`` hashes the Step's config and the
        incoming state, keys a class-level cache by
        ``(schema_version, hash)``, and reuses prior outputs on a
        hit. Requires ``_schema_version``.
    ``_schema_version`` — opaque string identifying the Step's
        output-relevant implementation version. Bumping invalidates
        all prior cache entries under the old version. Required when
        ``_cache == 'by_hash'``.

processes.name: RAMEmitter
processes.description:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).

processes.name: ResultsStep
processes.description:
The head of the post-sim Step family: reads a finished run's emitted
results location (store path(s), and optionally a sim_data reference)
from config or from a wired-in state input, and writes one
``ResultsHandle`` to the ``results`` store. Every downstream Step —
``AnalysisStep``, ``ReportCardStep``, etc. — reads from that single
handle, so a composite shaped ``[emitter output] -> ResultsStep ->
{AnalysisStep, ReportCardStep, ...}`` gives every post-sim Step the same
view of the run, computed once (``ResultsHandle`` caches its own
``.records()``/``.conn()``, so fan-out doesn't re-read the store).

Config keys (all optional): ``paths`` (list[str]), ``sim_data_ref``
(any), ``simulation_id`` (str). A same-named, non-empty ``state`` input
overrides the matching config key, so a composite can wire an upstream
store (e.g. a run-finished notification carrying the real output path)
instead of hard-coding a path in config.

A test (formerly "report card") as a visualization-like Step (sibling of

processes.name: ParquetEmitter
processes.description:
Generic Parquet emitter, hive-partitioned per ``partitioning_keys``.

The process-bigraph lifecycle drives the emit cadence:

  - configuration is written at ``__init__`` time from ``config["metadata"]``
    (only when ``metadata`` is non-None);
  - history rows arrive via ``update(state)`` per composite tick;
  - ``close(success=...)`` flushes the buffer and (when ``success=True``
    and a partitioning layout is configured) writes the success sentinel.

Durability-sensitive callers must call ``close()`` explicitly at end of
composite run; ``__del__`` calls it defensively but interpreter-shutdown
ordering is undefined.

processes.name: SQLiteEmitter
processes.description:
Append simulation state to a SQLite database each timestep.

One row per step, with the full state tree stored as JSON. The database
file is a single ``.db`` file that can be opened with any SQLite client,
queried with SQL, and kept for long-term storage. Multiple simulations
can share one file — rows are partitioned by ``simulation_id``.

To record the composite config or other metadata alongside the history
rows, call :func:`save_simulation_metadata` after constructing the
Composite — the emitter itself only writes the per-step history rows.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 = every
tick). The ``step`` column still stores the true composite tick number,
so time-series produced from the history reflect the real cadence even
though intermediate ticks were not persisted. Use this when a Composite
fires the emitter very often (small intervals, long runs) and you don't
need every tick in the archive — it's the cheapest way to shrink the
write volume without losing the simulation's time axis.

``batch_size`` buffers up to N recorded rows in memory and flushes them
in a single SQL transaction (default 1 = write each row immediately).
With ``batch_size=100`` the per-row fsync overhead is amortized across
the batch, giving a large speedup on high-frequency runs. Unflushed
rows are guaranteed to be written on ``close()`` and on the next
``query()``; a hard crash before flush loses the buffered rows.

processes.name: Tick
processes.description:
Accumulate continuous simulation time into a float ``t`` store.

Reads ``t`` and writes ``t + interval`` each update, where ``interval`` is
the process interval supplied by the engine. The starting value comes from
whatever the ``t`` store is initialized to in the composite state.
